Headteacher’s Welcome
“St. Ebbe’s is a vibrant school, full of love and joy, where adults and pupils flourish in a caring, supportive environment.” SIAMS Inspection March 2026
“Boredom has been confined to the past as imaginations are stretched by a multitude of opportunities, enabling ‘children to be children’ in a safe, exciting and inclusive way.” (Ofsted June 2024)
My name is Tina Farr and I am the proud Headteacher of St. Ebbe’s. I work alongside our Deputy and Co-Headteacher, Clare Whyles, who is Headteacher on Wednesdays.
Choosing a school for your child is one of the most important decisions you can make and may I thank you for visiting our website to find out more about us.
We believe we can offer your child something that is unique, where they will be valued for their individual passions and where they will truly belong. Our staff team are highly skilled at building the warm, trusting relationships that are essential for children to thrive.
We are committed to working with parents and our wider community to raise wise, compassionate citizens with the power to make a difference through our Core Values: Curiosity, Courage and Connection and through our journey to becoming a Rights Respecting School (currently Bonze Award holders).
We are a school with a culture rooted in compassion and love which transcends our approach to the curriculum and each interaction our staff has with you and your children. This is borne out through carefully chosen curriculum projects which are equally rich in knowledge and humanity.
Scroll down for several videos which will give you an insight into our lovely school and our approach to education as well as our recent feature on BBC Breakfast!
If you’d like to find out more, please contact our school office on 01865 248863 or email office.3833@st-ebbes.oxon.sch.uk, to book in a visit. I’d love to show you around so you can feel the St. Ebbe’s experience for yourselves and ask me every question you can think of!
Come and join us on our journey!
Tina Farr and Clare Whyles
“Belonging is being part of something bigger than yourself. But it’s also the courage to stand alone, and to belong to yourself above all else.”
An 8-minute Overview from me
A Day in the Life of a Reception Child
BBC News Feature – Our Warm Welcome
Our Curriculum
In this video, our Deputy Headteacher, Clare Whyles, explains about our ‘Curriculum of Hope’ Our beautifully constructed curriculum helps children remember knowledge because they care about the people in the places they study. More details can be found on our Curriculum Page.
Belonging and Being Unique
Each Thursday we hold a very special assembly, led by children and designed to give children the chance to share what they are passionate about.
Our Approach to Play
Play is essential for healthy child development. We take play seriously at St. Ebbe’s. Take a look at this video to understand our approach.
Our Green Space and Outdoor Provision
In this video, I talk about the importance of learning outdoors, Forest School and share the stunning grounds that are hidden away behind our school!
After School Club
Your child will be carefully looked after, inspired and engaged by our Wraparound Care from 3:15pm to 6:00pm. Check out this video for a flavour of our offer. More details can be found on our Wraparound Care page.
Here are 10 reasons why your child will thrive with us

pageCache.pageTitle: Performing Arts and Music – St Ebbes CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Music is a universal language that embodies one of the highest forms of creativity. Our Music curriculum will engage and inspire pupils, developing their love for and interest in many forms of music of different styles and from different times and cultures. It will develop their skills and confidence in taking part in music activities, in listening, singing and playing musical instruments. Music also makes an important contribution to the life of our school. It is embedded within our projects, taught mostly by a music specialist who also supports non-specialist delivery. See examples below.
Music Knowledge Progression
Singing
We have weekly Key-Stage 1 and 2 singing for all children: we sing a broad range of songs: in parts and in rounds, for assemblies, from musicals and linked to projects. We also listen to music from different cultures, times and in various styles.

pageCache.pageTitle: Is there any such thing as a good or bad person? – St Ebbes CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Is there any such thing as a good or bad person?
‘Person’: The troll & the giant
Place: Under the bridge & in the castle
Problem: The troll being angry with the billy goats & Jack stealing
Possibilities: That people have reasons for behaving the way that they do and that, if we are prepared to listen, we can understand each other better
This project will start with an angry troll who is frustrated by goats constantly ‘trip trapping’ over his bridge. The children will explore why he is feeling this way, and if we can find a solution to the problem. The children will read Billy Goats Fluff by Rachael Mortimer to see how the Billy Goat’s Grandma solves the problem by knitting the goats fluffy socks. The children will begin to discuss how the troll is feeling in relation to the ‘Zones of Regulation’ and relate this back to their own experiences of being in the ‘red zone’. After this, the children will take a similar approach to understanding how the giant is feeling in Jack and the Beanstalk. The children will seek to understanding why the Jack is so angry, and whether it was right for Jack to steal from the giant, even though he was poor. By the end of the project, the children will have a greater understanding of their own emotions, and the emotions of other people.
Trips out/Visitors In
A visit to the bridges in the local area.
A visit to the Oxford Castle.
The children performed a whole-class retelling of Jack and the Beanstalk to a huge audience of family and friends.
The children also shared their innovated alternative endings to Jack and the Beanstalk with their parents before they came to see the rest of their learning in class.
December 2023

pageCache.pageTitle: Wraparound Care – St Ebbes CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club (BFC)
Welcome to Breakfast Club! Breakfast Club is led by our smiley staff, Shami,Tracy & Hayley.
At St Ebbe’s we offer Breakfast Club daily, starting at 7.45am until 8.40am and provide a safe and stimulating environment for children before the start of a school day. It is designed to provide wraparound care for our working parents. Please note that children attending Breakfast Club should arrive before 8:15am.
Children are provided with a healthy and nutritious breakfast including cereal, wholemeal toast, and selection of fruits and juices. A range of activities such as arts & crafts and outdoor games are available every day, with the aim of ensuring that everyone is awake and ready for the day ahead.
Breakfast Club is staffed by our own Teaching Assistants. The cost is £4.50 per day for one child, £3.50 per day for additional siblings. This can be paid through Arbor or by cash to the office.
Bookings can all be made through your child’s Arbor account. Please follow the links for clubs.
Enquiries about Breakfast Club can be sent to clubs@st-ebbes.oxon.sch.uk
Available Voucher Schemes
After School Club (ASC)
Welcome to Our After School Club!
Are you looking for a safe, nurturing, and engaging environment for your child after school hours? Our After School Club is the perfect solution! Running from 3:15pm to 6pm, Monday to Friday, we offer a seamless transition from the school day to a home-like setting where your child can thrive.
At our After School Club, we live by our three core values: Curiosity, Courage, and Connection. These principles guide everything we do, ensuring that every moment spent with us contributes to your child’s growth and happiness.
Curiosity: We have wonderful play spaces which allows us to create an environment where curiosity is encouraged. Through diverse activities and exploration, we ignite your child’s love for learning and discovery.
Courage: Our club fosters a safe space where children are encouraged to take risks, try new things, and develop their confidence. We celebrate their successes and support them through challenges, helping them build resilience and a positive mindset.
Connection: Relationships are at the heart of our club. We ensure continuity and a deep understanding of your child’s individual needs, preferences, and abilities. Our team is passionate about creating meaningful connections, not just between staff and children, but also among the children themselves.
We understand the importance of continuity and familiarity for children. That’s why our team is primarily composed of TA leaders from our school, ensuring that your child is always in the care of familiar, trusted faces. This continuity helps us better understand and meet your child’s unique needs, making our club a true extension of their school day and a second home.
Our staff is dedicated to creating a warm, family-like atmosphere where every child feels valued and understood. We believe in the importance of play, creativity, and relaxation after a busy school day. Our range of activities includes arts and crafts, outdoor play, culinary skills, STEM and much more, ensuring that your child has a balanced and enjoyable experience.
Children are offered nutritious and healthy snacks/refreshments throughout their session. We change the snack menu weekly to allow children to explore new and exciting foods.
Choosing our After School Club means providing your child with a safe, enriching, and fun environment where they can grow, learn, and play. We are committed to supporting their learning journeys and helping them build the skills and relationships that will last a lifetime.
We invite you to visit us and see first hand the wonderful experiences we offer. Join our After School Club family today and give your child the gift of curiosity, courage, and connection.
Enquiries and new booking requests for After School Club can be sent to clubs@st-ebbes.oxon.sch.uk
Registrations and Booking Requests can be made using the ASC Registration and Booking Request Form if you are unable to book via Arbor.
Emergency one-off bookings for After School Club can be made via Arbor or by calling School Reception.

pageCache.pageTitle: Is water the most precious thing on Earth? – St Ebbes CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Is water the most precious thing on Earth?
Person: Kenyan Child
Place: Kenya, East Africa
Problem: Limited access to water
Possibilities: Advocating for the right to clean water across the planet, reducing our own water usage at school and home
Humans have the right to clean, fresh water but not everyone has enough. Through this project, the children learn about water inequality across the globe and what people are doing about it. They look at their own water usage, how it is used in the classroom, at school and at home, finding ways to reduce waste.
They undertake surveys and suggest ways of saving water efficiently. They will design posters and information leaflets to share this information with an audience of children and adults.
The children visit the local river habitat, alongside reading ‘A river’ and writing short stories as well as studying water depicted in art by Monet and Hokusai.
Discussions involve talking about water on the Earth and where it is found, distinguishing between salt and fresh water. Inequality, fairness and how humans fight for their right to clean water.
Trips out/Visitors In
Boat trip (June/July)
Water lilies in the Botanical gardens
Art Exhibition – an unveiling of a Monet ‘pond’ created outdoors, wonderful sea creatures and information shared about conserving and saving water.
“Beautiful work – and so wonderful to come into the school to see it. The care taken by the teachers to make children feel special about their work is amazing, e.g. framing the underwater animals artwork (like a proper exhibition!). And my son felt so proud having me in his space and giving me a tour, it was lovely. Thank you!” Year 2 Parent

pageCache.pageTitle: Personal Development – St Ebbes CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
At St. Ebbe’s, we combine PSHE (Personal, Social and Health Education) and RSE (Relationships and Sex Education) under the umbrella term: Personal Development.
Teaching healthy relationships is central to children becoming ‘wise, compassionate citizens’ who are able to appreciate and connect, rather than argue and fight, with others, even if they disagree. We use the ‘Lifewise’ scheme of work to teach children about respectful relationships: face to face and online friendships, staying safe in relationships with friends and adults, how to safely say no and the different family relationships that children may live within. We want every child in our school to feel accepted regardless of their ethnicity, religion, ability, family shape or any other characteristic: acceptance and kindness towards other people, even if our families, cultures and beliefs are different.

pageCache.pageTitle: P.E. and Sport – St Ebbes CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
At St Ebbe’s we want ALL children to have the opportunity to become physically literate and to find joy in movement, through high quality physical education, participation in organised sport and frequent engagement in activity.
We ask children to get up and move every 45 minutes to an hour by taking a walk or a run outside.
Regular physical activity is associated with improved learning and attainment and the benefits of exercise on an individual’s mental and physical health are indisputable. Participation in sport has the power to build empathy, tolerance and human connection and therefore is a key tool for the social and mental development of young people.
‘Real PE’ Scheme of Work
We use the ‘Real PE’ scheme of work at St. Ebbe’s because it is designed to include, challenge and support every child.
The lesson plans provide a structure for teachers to plan effective PE lessons which ensure progression and coverage of the core knowledge and skills of the National Curriculum.
Sports Competitions
We enter Sports Competitions such as Netball, Football, Cross Country and Athletics.
Clubs
Our staff offer Netball, Football, Athletics and Bollywood after school sports clubs. Please contact our school office for details of how to book on.
Physical Education Policy
Details of how we spend our Sports Premium can be found here.

pageCache.pageTitle: Science – St Ebbes CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Exciting Science lessons develop our children’s natural curiosity and wonder. Science teaching and learning at St Ebbe’s supports, encourages and challenges scientific thinking. As Albert Einstein said, ‘The important thing is to never stop questioning’.
Science brings together knowledge and awe and creates a love for continuous learning. In becoming thoughtful and critical scientists, children learn skills that they will use throughout their lives; they are able to make connections, question information and make careful and informed conclusions/opinions. They also learn and apply vital literacy, mathematics and ICT skills.
For the most part, Science is taught discretely from our Inquiry-Based Projects except where there are thoughtful and obvious links to be made.

pageCache.pageTitle: Enquiry-Based Projects – St Ebbes CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
“I love the way you teach our children, where empathy and real life experience play a fundamental role. I am also glad that you are making them aware of environmental problems without them feeling overwhelmed but empowered to make a change. Thank you!” Year 4 Parent
“We’re not ‘just kids’ at this school. It’s like there’s nothing ‘just’ about us. We are humans who have the power to make changes. Teachers support you and make you feel like you can do it. It’s a quality of this school that’s really nice.” Year 5 child.
Curriculum Intent
Children at St. Ebbe’s learn the disciplinary and substantive knowledge that define each curriculum subject, encapsulated by enquiry questions, which encourage them to think deeply, develop spiritually and want to further understand and to deepen the knowledge they encounter. (UNCRC Article 28)
‘You can travel the seas,poles and deserts and see nothing. To really understand the world, you need to get under the skin of the people and the places.’ Michael Palin
For more information about the sequencing of our enquiry questions, please click here.
Whilst learning each curriculum subject through our enquiry-based approach, children have multiple opportunities to encounter six themes: Sustainability, Courageous Advocacy, Leadership, Community, Belief and Creativity, themes which we believe will help them to become, ‘wise, compassionate citizens with the power to make a difference’.(UNCRC Article 28/29)
Reflecting our community, children learn about transformative, diverse individuals who have solved, or are solving the human problems they encounter and who have subsequently changed the world (UNCRC Article 2/17). Through this, children are inspired to make their own changes and to believe that, in the face of problems and uncertainty, they too can make a difference and be hopeful for a better future.
By presenting their work at Learning Exhibitions three times each year (UNCRC Article 12/13), children have the opportunity to refine their work so that it is the best they are capable of, to publicly express their knowledge and ideas orally and in in writing and through a variety of creative media, with the aim of inspiring other children and the adults in their lives to make changes and therefore be ‘of service to the world’.

pageCache.pageTitle: Is fire the most important discovery humankind ever made – St Ebbes CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Is fire the most important discovery humankind ever made?
Person: Thomas Farrinor
Place: Bakery in Pudding Lane, London
Problem: Bakery catches fire and sets light to wooden houses in East London
Possibilities: Rebuilding London and working as a team
The project begins with learning about why humans need fire and how it was created and how it was used/controlled in the past (pre-historic times and Indigenous peoples such as Native Americans and Aborigines) ) and compare this with how we use fire in the present day. The story, ‘How rabbit stole the fire’ is introduced gradually to encourage the children to think about who has a right to have fire – humans or animals? Can humans and animals share our planet and all that it has to offer?
The second part of this project starts with the history of the Great Fire of London and the story of Thomas Farrinor’s bakery in Pudding Lane. Historical figures such as Samuel Pepys, John Evelyn and William Taswell are studied to discover the importance of diaries as a historical primary source. Paintings and drawings are studied to observe London in 1666.
To encourage children to think about the beauty and danger of fire we create a variety of poems (Kennings, Acrostic, Calligrams). Artwork focuses on recreating the Great Fire of London scene.
Children are taught about fire safety by writing instructions for a fire drill and speaking to local firefighters.
Trips out/Visitors In
Science Oxford – The Great Fire of London workshop
A Fire Poetry book launch where children share their poems with parents and carers.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art – St Ebbes CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Art, craft and design embody some of the highest forms of human creativity. A high-quality art and design education should engage, inspire, and challenge pupils, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to experiment, invent and create their own works of art. Pupils should know about great artists and designers and have the opportunity to evaluate and analyse creative works using the language of art, craft and design. As pupils progress, they should be able to think critically and develop a more rigorous understanding of art and design. They should also know how art and design both reflect and shape our history, and contribute to the culture, creativity, and wealth of our nation.

pageCache.pageTitle: Can we future-proof our planet? – St Ebbes CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
Can we future-proof our planet?
The family on a roof surrounded by flood-water
The person on a car in Grandpont
Grandpont, Oxford, UK
How do we help him and his community to cope with perpetual flooding?
How do we cope with perpetual flooding in Oxford?
Floating farms, stilt houses, looking more broadly at human adaptations to environments.
Local solutions to controlling flooding in Oxford.
The project starts with a narrative built around a family on a roof in Bangladesh where there is perpetual flooding and makes the link between flooding and climate change. Through the study of geography, we compare the human and physical features of Grandpont, Oxford, Lynmouth (Devon) and Bangladesh and how these factors have contributed to flooding in both areas as well as human-centred design that have led to innovative solutions to this increasing problem. We will learn about rivers and river systems, including the River Thames and the River Lyn, Devon (Great Flood of 1952).
More detail to follow.

pageCache.pageTitle: Computing – St Ebbes CofE Primary School
pageCache.text:
With technology advancing at an ever-increasing rate, it is important that we equip the next generation with the necessary skills to navigate the technical world safely. At St. Ebbe’s Primary School, we want to ensure that our children have the confidence to use technology positively and responsibly, and set high expectations for our behaviour in the virtual world.
We recognise the need for agile thinkers and risk takers; and will endeavour to encourage and foster the innovation and creativity needed for an unknown technical future.
